content.overview:
## A section library Marketing could build with I planned and led Shopify Plus migrations for [AOP](https://aop.com) and [Ignite Christian Academy](https://www.ignitechristianacademy.com). Marketing needed to build campaigns without waiting for each page to be coded. I built the Liquid sections and their Shopify editor controls: reusable layouts with editable content, media, spacing, actions and mobile behavior. The library replaced marketing functionality that would otherwise have depended on paid apps.

Explore all custom sections

The full gallery preserves the development examples, including placeholder copy and layout variants. The crops below show individual patterns alongside finished storefront examples. ## Tabs that handle more than one layout The tab section supports text or icon navigation, horizontal or vertical layouts, media panels and accordion content. Editors choose the arrangement and populate each tab without changing the section code. ![Icon navigation, a media panel and configurable actions in the custom Shopify tab section](sections-tabs.webp) On AOP, that section becomes a subject browser. Each selection reveals curriculum information and an action for that subject. ## Tokens, components and page layouts The design-system gallery follows the shared tokens, an editable benefit card, section variants, page layouts and a finished storefront. Orange action colors, Caladea headings, Open Sans content and repeated spacing rules carry through the components. The section schema exposes layout controls; repeatable tab blocks hold the labels, imagery, copy and actions. Liquid renders those choices, with CSS scoped to the section instance. ![Brand rules, Shopify schema controls and three rendered tab layouts showing how one section stays reusable](section-contract.webp) That structure lets Marketing change a page's content and arrangement while the component stays maintainable. The [style and schema snapshot](/demo/shopify/design-system-tokens.json) includes examples of the actual settings. ### Try the component This browser prototype demonstrates the tab structure, layout choices and keyboard behavior. The production section runs in Shopify Liquid. ## More sections from the library ### Benefits and content grids Repeated blocks combine images or icons, headings, copy and actions. Editors control the card treatment, spacing and layout, including a side-scroll option. ![Two benefit cards from the development gallery, with image, copy and different action treatments](sections-cards.webp) ### Media and product explanations Image-and-text sections handle product details, screenshots and video. Alignment and mobile spacing are configurable. This example is from AOP's finished Monarch page. ![The custom media-and-text section explaining Monarch on the finished AOP storefront](sections-content.webp) ### Campaign calls to action The gallery includes contained and full-width treatments, image and video backgrounds, and light and dark variants. Primary and secondary actions give each campaign a clear next step. ![A dark campaign call-to-action variant from the original development gallery](sections-cta.webp) ## Built into two Shopify Plus storefronts The page mockups show how the finished AOP sections fit together at desktop and phone sizes, from the hero and product explanation to benefits and subject detail. ![Desktop and phone page-layout studies composed from the finished AOP marketing sections](page-mockups.webp) Ignite's landing page brings campaign messaging and a lead form into the same hero. Farther down, the comparison section helps families understand the school options. ![Ignite's finished campaign hero with a lead-capture form](sections-lead-form.webp) ![The reusable comparison table on Ignite's finished school overview page](sections-comparison.webp) AOP used Kalles; Ignite used Horizon. I also built jump navigation, custom dropdown navigation and a footer, plus dynamic product-detail and collection templates for Ignite. Client designers and marketers chose the final artwork, copy, section order and brand color use. I kept the custom work additive, handled production fixes and support, and worked with GTM, GA4, Shopify Analytics, Shoplift and Crazy Egg for measurement. [View AOP's Monarch page](https://aop.com/pages/monarch), [visit Ignite's school overview](https://www.ignitechristianacademy.com/pages/online-school-overview), or [open the technical design-system study](/demo/shopify/shopify-design-system.pdf).
